conbody.p: Add task makes a card in the board's To Do column and places it on the plan, with a start and a due date if you give them. Or add one in the chart itself: type a title in the last row of the outline, Add a task…, and press Enter. The task appears as a new row with no dates, ready to be scheduled on the timeline.
To move a task, drag its bar. To change one date, drag that end of the bar. Both move in whole days.
To place a task that has no dates, use its empty row on the timeline:

ul.li: Click a date, and the task is scheduled for the period of the scale that holds it: that day at Days, that week at Weeks, that month at Months, that quarter at Quarters. The row shows the period as you point at it.
Drag across the row, and the task is scheduled for the range you drag over, drawn as it grows with its dates beside it.

conbody.p: Select a task, by its title in the outline or by its bar, to see it beside the chart. Open the full task in that panel, like the open button on the row, shows everything else about it. In the panel you can:

ul.li: set its Start and Due dates, its Duration and its Effort: see Duration and effort. The due date is the card's own, so the board shows the same day;
make it a sub-task of another task, or a top-level task again;
assign it to a milestone: see Assigning tasks to a milestone;
set its relationships to other tasks, whichever of the two drives;
add to-dos and tick them off;

conbody.p: Sub-task of and the task chooser under Relationships are searchable: open one and type part of a task's name or its outline number to narrow a long plan to the task you want.
A task cannot start after it is due, or be a sub-task of one of its own sub-tasks.
